messages:
anya: Heads-up — Safety scan flagged CVE-2026-3456 in tokenizers wheel (manylinux build) and our main CI started failing on wheel install this morning.
security-bot: [alert] CVE-2026-3456 tokenizers < 0.16.5 — severity: medium — affected: linux wheel builds — link: https://nvd.example/CVE-2026-3456
anya: CI failure is on ubuntu-latest runner during pip install: 
```
ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement tokenizers==0.16.5 (from -r requirements.txt (line 12))
ERROR: No matching distribution found for tokenizers==0.16.5
```
We pinned to 0.16.5 in the lock yesterday when running a local build; looks like manylinux wheel upload was missing for 0.16.5 for some platforms.
omar: I reproduced locally in a clean container (manylinux2014) — tokenizers 0.16.5 wheel absent, falls back to sdist build but that requires rust toolchain and fails in our wheel-build CI step. Quick bisect shows tokenizers roll at commit c3f2d7 bumped build pipeline.
sam: So we have two problems: the CVE (needs a fix) and the CI break (wheel unavailability). Which do we prioritize? The CVE implies we should not pin to an older vulnerable release.
liam: Suggestion: triage path — 1) Confirm whether 0.16.5 actually contains the CVE fix. If yes, we need that version but CI fails to fetch wheel; 2) If upstream release is broken (missing wheel), open support ticket with upstream and fallback to patch: apply backported security patch to our vendored copy or pin to 0.16.4 + local patch and mark as temporary with a rollback plan.
anya: I checked release notes — 0.16.5 claims the fix but the manylinux artifact was omitted for linux/x86_64 on PyPI (seen in our artifact index). So safe version exists but distribution incomplete.
omar: I'll open an issue against tokenizers and ping maintainers. In parallel we can do a short-lived workaround: rebuild tokenizers wheel in our CI and cache it in artifact storage for the org. That avoids changing dependency graph.
sam: Rebuilding wheel in CI requires rust toolchain in our build image — that's heavy and slows CI. Alternative: create a temporary package index (artifact bucket) and upload a manually-built manylinux wheel (signed) and point CI at it until upstream fixes PyPI.
liam: Operational concerns: needs KMS upload signing and audit log entry. We should use the org KMS key to sign the artifact and add an entry in the security audit log. Also add an RBAC grant for devops CI user for artifact write, short TTL.
anya: Proposed action items: 
- omar: open upstream issue + ping maintainers (ETA 1h).
- sam: prototype wheel build + upload pipeline to our private index (artifact-bucket) and add signing step using KMS (ETA end of day).
- liam: draft audit log entry + RBAC grant for the temp CI role, coordinate with people-ops for expiration (ETA today).
- anya: prepare PR that pins poetry.lock to tokenizers==0.16.5 if we host a wheel, and include mitigation notes and revert plan.

omar: Created GH issue https://github.com/tokenizers/tokenizers/issues/9999 — pinged maintainers, included CI logs and exact missing artifact names. @maintainers please advise.
security-bot: [note] label added: vulnerability, needs-triage
sam: Quick experiment: built wheel locally with `docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/work quay.io/pypa/manylinux2014_x86_64 /bin/bash -c "pip wheel /work/tokenizers-0.16.5.tar.gz -w /work/wheels"` then uploaded to staging bucket. Local test passes `pip install --index-url https://staging.pkgs.internal/simple tokenizers==0.16.5` and our app imports fine.
liam: Good. Before we publish to CI index we need a signed artifact and an audit record. I'll add an entry in the security audit spreadsheet and set a 7-day TTL on the PKG write permission.
anya: For the poetry/pip lock update: if we host the wheel in internal index temporarily, we should update `poetry.lock` and `requirements.txt` to point to tokenizers==0.16.5 and include a comment referencing the temporary index + revert instructions.
sam: I'll open a draft PR with the lock regenerations and the CI change to `pip config set global.extra-index-url https://staging.pkgs.internal/simple` behind a deploy flag. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4123 (draft).
omar: Also think about backporting a minimal security patch to 0.16.4 if upstream is slow — but that increases maintenance burden. Marking that as plan B.
liam: I'll coordinate with security ops to ensure KMS signing uses HSM-backed key and we log the operation to Splunk. Also preparing RBAC short-lived role for CI: `artifact-writer-temp` with expiry.
anya: Priority: P1 (affects hosted builds and has an associated CVE). Let's tag the PRs accordingly and schedule a short incident-style oncall overlap for the roll (so we can revert quickly if something breaks).
devops-bot: Deploy checklist created: `#4123` needs approvals from `eng-sre`, `eng-security`, and `devex` before enabling index change in CI.
sam: I'll run full test matrix on a branch after wheel is uploaded; ETA 2-3 hours. omar will keep posting upstream status.
omar: Upstream replied: "we're re-uploading missing manylinux wheels, ETA 4 hours" — posted link to their upload job. Marking status: monitoring.
anya: OK, moving to action. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
